rows.title: CT on pace for tiny $6 million budget deficit, Comptroller projects
rows.standfirst: CT Comptroller Sean Scanlon projected that Gov. Ned Lamont is months away from the first formal budget deficit of his administration.

rows.title: Medicaid uncertainty looms over new CT hospital tax deal talks
rows.standfirst: As the hospital industry seeks a new multiyear financial arrangement with CT, both are threatened by huge cuts in federal Medicaid assistance.

rows.title: Towns to CT: We need bigger share of casino slot machine revenue
rows.standfirst: Advocates want a 50-50 split in casino slot revenues, saying it would help restore towns to the level of support they received decades ago.

rows.title: Lamont, CT lawmakers could use more good luck this tax season
rows.standfirst: As final negotiations on the next CT budget get underway, Gov. Ned Lamont and his fellow Democrats in the legislature have a big problem.

rows.title: Lamont delivers pledged raises to CT state employees
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont has now reached tentative deals with unions and can ask lawmakers to approve raises for the bulk of CT’s unionized workforce.

rows.title: House GOP budget offers big relief but works around spending cap
rows.standfirst: The CT GOP plan relies on shifting millions in hospital payments outside the spending cap and on CT winning a legal battle against New York.

rows.title: Working class advocates call for CT Billionaire’s Tax
rows.standfirst: About a dozen people dressed as Mr. Monopoly spent Tax Day at Gov. Ned Lamont’s office, asking for a fairer tax system.

rows.title: Officials plan to tap savings to make next CT budget work
rows.standfirst: The move would ensure Connecticut’s next budget provides major boosts to municipal aid, affordable child care and tax relief.

rows.title: Report: Most states ignore ‘tax gap’ that CT is trying to close
rows.standfirst: Officials weren’t thrilled last year to learn CT has a nearly $3 billion difference between taxes owed to the state and actual collections.

rows.title: Senate GOP won’t show how it would balance next CT budget
rows.standfirst: Senate Republicans, the caucus that has proposed far more tax relief than any other, has decided to play their cards close to the vest.

rows.title: CT officials struggle to pay for school aid even without tax rebate
rows.standfirst: CT leaders are focused on investments in schools, child care and hospitals, even if it means scrapping a proposed $200-per-person tax rebate.

rows.title: How do CT municipalities adopt, pay for their budgets?
rows.standfirst: While CT funds its budget off a mix of taxes, including income, sales, business and more – towns get most of their money from property taxes.

rows.title: With Lamont, Democrats at odds, GOP can shape next CT budget
rows.standfirst: With Democrats at odds over how to balance CT’s budget, the door is open for minority Republicans to shape the state’s fiscal future.

rows.title: Legislators, Lamont on cusp of tentative CT budget deal
rows.standfirst: The compromise plan to aid schools and hospitals in the next CT budget was to be shared with rank-and-file lawmakers Monday night.

rows.title: Lamont moves quickly to tout new CT budget deal
rows.standfirst: Lamont said $270 million in municipal aid included in the deal would be available to towns even if they’ve already adopted a local budget.

rows.title: CT legislature OKs raises for unionized state employees
rows.standfirst: The legislature approved contracts Wednesday that would grant 2.5% annual cost-of-living raises for most CT state employees through 2028.

rows.title: Can CT be more affordable without major tax cuts?
rows.standfirst: Democratic leaders say town aid and child care investments will pay big dividends, even without tax rebates or a child tax credit.

rows.title: Last-minute revenue surge makes path to new CT budget easier
rows.standfirst: Analysts estimate that surging income tax receipts and other revenue would add about $580 million to CT’s coffers this fiscal year and next.
